official.deadline_note: There is no central deadline: 'Acceptance to a PhD-programme is done continuously throughout the academic year and is not restricted to the beginning of term.' Each individual vacancy announced on NTNU's web pages and on jobbnorge.no carries its own application deadline.
official.application_cycle: Continuous admission throughout the academic year; individual PhD vacancies are posted and closed on their own schedules
official.status_note: Admission is assessed continuously as vacancies are announced, so a position can open and close at any point in the year rather than within a fixed application window.
official.tuition_coverage_note: 'Unlike in most other countries, PhD candidates in Norway are not considered students and PhD candidates are usually employees of the institution from which they receive their funding.' 'Most PhD candidates at NTNU are employed as PhD research fellows (stipendiat) at NTNU or a university college.'
benefits: Salaried employment as a PhD research fellow (stipendiat) at NTNU or a university college, rather than a student grant
Norwegian public-sector pension and employee benefit schemes through employment
Counselling services from NTNU International Researcher Support (NIRS) for administrative and relocation matters, and for people considering NTNU as a workplace

Funding can also come from an agreement with your regular employer, the Research Council of Norway under the Industrial PhD or Public sector PhD schemes, or other national or international scholarships
eligibility: Completed at least five years of higher education that includes a master's degree or other equivalent degree
A strong academic record and a weighted average for the last two years of your master's degree equivalent to a B or higher in NTNU's grading scale
A funding plan: financing is an absolute requirement for acceptance to a PhD programme at NTNU
At least two academic supervisors, at least one of whom, usually the main supervisor, must be employed at NTNU, including for externally funded candidates
Education from outside Norway may require NOKUT recognition or a faculty-level assessment; the individual faculty or programme may set further qualification requirements
requirements: Secure a funding plan covering the entire PhD period before acceptance
Get in touch with the research group and find a potential supervisor as early in the process as possible, with the main supervisor ready when you apply
Prepare the application in cooperation with your main supervisor and send it to the faculty through the department
Use NTNU's fixed application form in addition to the listed attachments, unless the individual faculty or programme has its own form
documents: Documentation of former education qualifying you for a PhD, along with any diploma supplement and/or NOKUT assessment if available
Documentation of education obtained outside of Norway
Documentation of funding for the entire PhD period
Project description, either complete or preliminary; if a preliminary description is accepted, a complete version must be made available within six months of admission
Details of any legal or ethical issues related to the project, with ethics committee or other approval enclosed where possible
selection_criteria: A strong academic record and a weighted average for the last two years of the master's degree equivalent to a B or higher in NTNU's grading scale
A confirmed funding plan for the whole PhD period, since financing is an absolute requirement for acceptance
At least two academic supervisors with at least one employed at NTNU
The individual faculty or programme may set further qualification requirements
coverage: Salary as an NTNU employee (PhD research fellow / stipendiat) under the Norwegian state pay scale, as set out in the individual vacancy
Pension and employee benefit schemes through employment
No separate tuition, travel or accommodation funding is published on these pages
application_method: Apply to an individually advertised PhD vacancy; positions are announced on NTNU's web pages and through jobbnorge.no
The application is written up in cooperation with the main supervisor and sent to the faculty through the department
official.application_route: Apply to an individually advertised PhD vacancy on NTNU's vacancy pages or jobbnorge.no, with the application prepared together with the main supervisor and submitted to the faculty through the department.
official.citizenship_residency: No citizenship or residency restriction is published on NTNU's admission and financing page
official.international_eligibility: International applicants are eligible; education obtained outside Norway may need NOKUT recognition or a faculty-level assessment
official.research_requirement: A project description, complete or preliminary, must accompany the application; if a preliminary description is accepted a complete version must be made available within six months of admission. Legal or ethical issues related to the project should be detailed, with ethics committee or other approval enclosed where possible.
official.duration: Three-year full-time study as standard; some positions include a fourth year of required duties, usually teaching, as detailed in the employee contract
official.description: NTNU's PhD positions are salaried employment rather than scholarships: candidates are normally employed as PhD research fellows (stipendiat), and financing for the entire PhD period is an absolute requirement for acceptance. Admission requires at least five years of higher education including a master's degree and a strong academic record, and is handled continuously through individually advertised vacancies.
official.program_type: Doctoral employment position (PhD research fellow / stipendiat)

not_confirmed: salary or stipend level for PhD research fellows
tuition, travel and accommodation coverage figures
verification.notes: Admission requirements, the funding-plan requirement, the employee rather than student status of PhD candidates, supervision rules, the continuous admission process and the application document list were all read on NTNU's own PhD pages. NTNU publishes no salary figure for stipendiat positions on those pages, and individual vacancies vary, so no amount is recorded.

applicant_utility.summary: There is no central application and no central deadline, so the real work is finding a supervisor and a funded project before you ever apply; NTNU will not accept you without a funding plan for the whole period. In practice that means landing an advertised stipendiat post or bringing employer, Industrial PhD or Public Sector PhD money with you. Because you would be an employee rather than a student, expect employee paperwork, Norwegian tax and pension arrangements rather than student immigration.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Master's graduates with a B-or-better weighted average, a concrete research idea and a named supervisor willing to co-write the application.
application_readiness_checklist: Map potential supervisors by browsing department and research group pages before contacting anyone
Secure a main supervisor who is already on board before you submit anything
Sort out funding early: an advertised stipendiat post, an agreement with your regular employer, or an Industrial or Public Sector PhD scheme
Start a NOKUT assessment or a faculty-level assessment of foreign credentials well ahead of any vacancy deadline
Draft a project description solid enough that a final version can follow within six months of admission
common_rejection_risks: Applying without a funding plan, which is an absolute bar to acceptance
Applying without a main supervisor in place, or with fewer than two academic supervisors
A weighted average in the last two master's years below a B on NTNU's scale
A preliminary project description that is never upgraded within six months of admission
Missing an ethics or data-protection approval the project depends on
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Relocation, housing and settling-in costs. The published pages state no tuition, travel or accommodation support, and the salary level is set by the individual vacancy rather than by the programme.
document_audit: Diploma supplements matter here, since NTNU asks for them alongside degree documentation
Foreign credentials need either a NOKUT assessment or a faculty-level one, and both take time
Evidence of funding must cover the entire PhD period, not just the first year
Project descriptions and any ethics approvals travel with the application, so prepare them before a deadline appears
Check whether the target faculty or programme uses its own application form in addition to NTNU's fixed form
alerts: Acceptance is continuous all year, so a vacancy can close at any moment and the next one may not match your field
Some positions carry a fourth year of duties, usually teaching, which is set out in the employee contract
At least one supervisor, usually the main one, must be employed at NTNU even for externally funded candidates
Positions are advertised on jobbnorge.no as well as on ntnu.edu, so monitor both
The PhD also includes at least 30 ECTS of coursework alongside a thesis estimated at 2.5 years of work
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Apply to a specific vacancy, with the application written together with the main supervisor and routed to the faculty through the department, then assessed continuously rather than in a single round.
